goal: In 90 seconds, show what an eigenvector is: the directions a matrix does not turn — with one 2x2 example computed, not asserted.
audience: a student who knows matrix multiplication but has never seen why eigenvectors matter
assumptions: 90 seconds means the finished film, first word to last frame
narrated means a voice throughout with captions on
the two formats are re-compositions, not crops
the language is English: the narration and every on-screen word follow the request
captions accompany the narration (English, monotonic SRT) as a deliverable
one audio mix at the studio loudness target with the narration intelligible
narrated: continuous spoken narration with a real audio stream throughout

decision.why: The piece shows a matrix acting on vectors with the eigen equation Av = lambda v computed on screen; every number must be a verified claim (the characteristic polynomial, the eigenvalues) and the narration must drive the scenes — the math technique's sympy claims and narration clock are exactly that.

alternatives.rejected_because: code-drawn motion could animate the arrows, but every number on screen (det, trace, the eigenvalues) would need hand-verification per frame — the math kind verifies claims mechanically

alternatives.id: simplest: one static frame per step with captions
alternatives.rejected_because: the simplest thing that could work — a slideshow — but the payoff (the vector NOT turning while everything else does) is motion; a static frame cannot land it

segments.brief: The directions a matrix does not turn: one 2x2 matrix, its action on the plane, the eigen equation with the eigenvalues computed, and why it matters in one line.
acceptance: every number on screen is a sympy-verified claim
the narration clock drives the scenes
explains eigenvectors themselves — the intuition: the vector a transformation scales but never rotates
every on-screen mathematical claim is verified (sympy)
the 9:16 deliverable is composed for vertical (format-aware re-layout, safe area)
the segment durations sum to the 90 s target
narration and on-screen text in English

risks: the 9:16 re-composition must not cramp the plane
the eigen example must be small enough to verify on screen in 90s
